A correctness release. **If you are running the 0.5.0 Windows build, replace it** —
that binary had two defects, both described below. Linux 0.5.0 is unaffected by
the first and clean on the second; upgrading is still worthwhile for the guard.

No functional changes to the VPN itself. Same wire protocol, same config format,
same commands as 0.5.0.

## Which file

| You have | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux, normal PC or server | `nospoon-linux-x86_64-release.tar.gz` |
| Linux on ARM — Raspberry Pi, NanoPi, most SBCs | `nospoon-linux-aarch64-release.tar.gz` |
| Windows 10/11 | `nospoon-windows-x86_64-release.zip` |

Every download is self-contained: unpack and run. Linux binaries are statically
linked against musl, so `ldd` says "not a dynamic executable" and the same file
runs on Debian, Alpine, Raspberry Pi OS or a distroless container. Windows ships
`nospoon.exe` plus `wintun.dll` and needs no Visual C++ Redistributable.

The `-debug` builds are the same binary with verbose DHT logging to stderr.
**Debug output includes peer IP addresses** — do not paste it in public
unredacted. macOS is not attached; build it from source via the flake or CMake.

## What was wrong with 0.5.0 on Windows

**It was built against libuv 1.52.1.** libuv 1.52.0 changed how a UDP socket's
error state is handled: an ICMP "fragmentation needed" from a smaller-MTU path
latches an error that is then never cleared. Sends keep failing, no retransmit
timer fires, and an established tunnel wedges in the "connected" state with no
data and no self-heal. It is intermittent and depends on the network path, so it
does not show up on a LAN test — which is why it was not caught. Windows now
builds against libuv 1.51.0, pinned.

The Linux builds were never affected: the Nix flake pins a nixpkgs that ships
1.51.0, and that pin has been there all along. Only the Windows and macOS jobs
resolved libuv at build time, and nothing checked the result.

**The Windows "release" binary had debug logging compiled in.** It carried the
verbose DHT log strings, including ones that format peer IP addresses. The
release build is now verified to contain none. If you ran the 0.5.0 Windows
build and captured its stderr anywhere — a log file, a service wrapper, a
pasted bug report — that output may contain peer addresses.

## What changed

- The build now **refuses** to compile against a libuv known to have the bug,
  rather than warning. This covers every path: Nix, all three CI platforms, and
  a plain end-user `cmake`. A version that has not been validated warns instead
  of failing, so a future fixed libuv is not blocked.
- Every CI job now asserts what its own artifact claims — that a release build
  contains no debug logging, that a Linux binary has no dynamic dependencies,
  that a Windows binary imports only DLLs present on a stock system. Previously
  only some jobs did, and the platform that checked was the platform that was
  already correct.
- Linux release binaries are built on native runners for each architecture
  rather than cross-compiled.

## Flake outputs

`packages.<system>` now contains only outputs native to that system:
`nospoon-cpp`, `nospoon-cpp-debug`, `nospoon-js`, and `default`. The
cross-compiled attributes — `nospoon-cpp-x86_64`, `nospoon-cpp-aarch64`,
`nospoon-cpp-aarch64-static` and their `-debug` variants — are **gone**. If you
referenced one, use the per-system path instead:

```
nix build .#packages.aarch64-linux.nospoon-cpp
```

`services.nospoon.package` and anything pinning `packages.<system>.nospoon-cpp`
are unaffected.

## Known issues

- **Single-stream transfer speed is well below the link.** Traced to the
  delivery-rate estimator in the UDX transport, which uses millisecond
  timestamps — too coarse on a low-latency path. It is not nospoon's encryption,
  framing, or your hardware: raw UDX reproduces it with none of nospoon in the
  path, and the JavaScript implementation shows the same behaviour. A fix is
  being worked on upstream and is not in this release.
- **Hole punching still fails on some carrier paths**, typically symmetric CGNAT
  on mobile. `nospoon check <client-config>` reports `HOLEPUNCH_FAILED (-5)`.
  Retrying or changing network usually works; there is no relay fallback yet.
- **Shutting down a client that never connected** trips an assertion in the
  transport layer and exits noisily instead of cleanly. Harmless — it happens on
  the way out — and it does not affect a client that did connect.

## Verifying your download

```
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```
